responsibility_alignment.rule: Missing E2 official rubric cannot excuse local false acceptance; E2 evidence metrics feed the E1 six-dimensional score and do not form a separate total.

findings.observed: The E2 metric-level official rubric is unsigned; the current synthetic rubric can only produce a partial diagnostic score.
findings.impact: No score can be treated as an official acceptance result.
findings.close_condition: Bind a signed official rubric to the frozen contract and rerun formula, boundary, and determinism tests.

findings.observed: The runner publishes raw success and COMPLETED before validator/scorer completion; integration can only fail closed afterward.
findings.impact: Different artifacts can report conflicting terminal states.
findings.close_condition: Validate and score before publishing success, then atomically bind result, score, manifest, archive, and marker.

findings.observed: Empty anomaly CSV and GeoJSON still passed the hard gate with no failed checks and a diagnostic score of 90.
findings.impact: Missing anomaly outputs can be accepted.
findings.close_condition: Require exactly one anomaly decision per valid observation and bidirectional consistency with GeoJSON.

findings.observed: SQLite observation values were changed to contradict CSV while preserving row count; validation still passed with a diagnostic score of 90.
findings.impact: Conflicting scientific records can be accepted.
findings.close_condition: Compare both stores bidirectionally by observation identity and all scientific fields.

findings.observed: Run, config, and contract identities in manifests were changed to different or invalid values; validation still passed with a diagnostic score of 90.
findings.impact: Results can be detached from their frozen inputs and contract.
findings.close_condition: Require equality across result, artifact manifest, run manifest, and resolved config, and recompute all declared hashes.

findings.observed: A source JSONL record containing a duplicate source_id key was silently accepted with a diagnostic score of 90.
findings.impact: Ambiguous provenance records can change meaning across parsers.
findings.close_condition: Use duplicate-key-rejecting JSON decoding for every line and test duplicate critical provenance fields.

findings.observed: A QC check explicitly set to fail still passed the scientific hard gate with a diagnostic score of 90.
findings.impact: Known scientific quality failures can be scored as acceptable.
findings.close_condition: Freeze fail/warn semantics so fail triggers a P0 gate and warn is consistent with partial status and limitation disclosure.

findings.observed: An H3 cell was replaced with 000000000000000; validation still passed with a diagnostic score of 90.
findings.impact: Invalid spatial indexing and map linkage can be accepted.
findings.close_condition: Validate index and resolution with an independent H3 implementation and recompute cells from coordinates.

findings.observed: A source row and referenced file/document were changed to nonexistent objects while retaining syntactically valid hashes; validation still passed with a diagnostic score of 90.
findings.impact: Fabricated or unresolvable provenance can be accepted.
findings.close_condition: Open and hash frozen source files and verify row, sample, version, document, and report bindings.

interpretation: The value 90 is an external synthetic-rubric diagnostic emitted for intentionally corrupted fixtures. It is evidence of false acceptance, not a Benchmark v6 task score or an official E1 six-dimensional score.
